main_body: A three-tier gray stone/metal shelf stand with rows of small candles on each tier, plus a dark base plinth at the bottom
top_band: none: each tier is a 1-row light gray line (L=170) over a 1-row dark line (L=61); there is no multi-row horizontal surface
evidence: The column scan shows each tier is only a 1px light edge (L=170) and a 1px dark line (L=61). Each shelf is a thin line seen edge-on and none shows a top surface, so the shelf tops are not visible from above. The candles stand on the lines in plain front view. The tiers are open gaps, so there is no front face either. The 16px-wide drawing reads as a front elevation of a rack, matching the guide's 'rim only' and 'front elevation' red examples. The bottom base is a flat dark block with a 1px highlight and has no top surface.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours against 38-40 for the references. The shelves are 2-3 tone lines with no grain or texture. The candles have a small warm ramp (white, yellow, orange), but the stand itself is a thin gray line with a dark line below it and has no material shading. The dark edge pixels are mostly tinted (9% neutral), so the outline is acceptable, but overall the piece is much sparser and flatter than the stall and well references.
